intended_object: The canonical morphism K → τ^{≥n}K from a ℤ-indexed cochain complex onto its canonical truncation in degrees ≥ n (inferred from the docstring, the name and the module doc), which induces isomorphisms on cohomology in degrees ≥ n.
explanation: The body is exactly the general Mathlib construction HomologicalComplex.πTruncGE, applied to the embedding embeddingUpIntGE n. That embedding sends ℕ to the integers ≥ n, so the truncation keeps degrees ≥ n, and the target matches the abbreviation CochainComplex.truncGE. The lemma quasiIsoAt_πTruncGE in the same file shows the map is a quasi-isomorphism in every degree q ≥ n, as expected. The hypotheses are the right ones: zero morphisms, a zero object, and homology in every degree. The definition is a convenience specialisation of the general construction to ℤ-indexed cochain complexes, the standard setting for canonical truncations in the literature. It does not rewrite the construction in a special case, so it is not too narrow.
